questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzene is treated with 3 H2 / Pt catalyst (2000 psi, 100°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzene with 3 H2 / Pt catalyst (2000 psi, 100°C) yields Cyclohexane. Rationale: Extreme pressure and temperature are required to overcome the 150 kJ/mol aromatic resonance stabilization energy.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzene into 1,4-Cyclohexadiene?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzene into 1,4-Cyclohexadiene, the appropriate reagent is Na metal, liquid NH3, ethanol. Rationale: Stepwise radical-anion reduction reduces benzene to an unconjugated, non-aromatic 1,4-diene.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Methoxybenzene (anisole) is treated with Na, liquid NH3, ethanol?
questions.explanation: Treating Methoxybenzene (anisole) with Na, liquid NH3, ethanol yields 1-Methoxy-1,4-cyclohexadiene. Rationale: Electron-donating methoxy group directs protonation so that the methoxy-bearing carbon is not reduced.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzoic acid into 2,5-Cyclohexadiene-1-carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzoic acid into 2,5-Cyclohexadiene-1-carboxylic acid, the appropriate reagent is Na, liquid NH3, ethanol. Rationale: Electron-withdrawing carboxyl group directs reduction such that the carbon bearing -COOH receives a proton.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Toluene (methylbenzene) is treated with KMnO4 / H2O / heat then acid?
questions.explanation: Treating Toluene (methylbenzene) with KMnO4 / H2O / heat then acid yields Benzoic acid + MnO2. Rationale: Benzylic C-H bonds are uniquely susceptible to exhaustive permanganate oxidation into benzoic acid.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Ethylbenzene into (1-Bromoethyl)benzene + Succinimide?
questions.explanation: To convert Ethylbenzene into (1-Bromoethyl)benzene + Succinimide, the appropriate reagent is NBS / light / CCl4. Rationale: Bromination occurs exclusively at the benzylic position due to resonance stabilization of the benzylic radical.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Sodium hydride (NaH) to yield Sodium cyclopentadienide (aromatic 6 pi-electron ring) + H2 as the major product?
questions.explanation: Cyclopentadiene (pKa 16) reacts with Sodium hydride (NaH) to yield Sodium cyclopentadienide (aromatic 6 pi-electron ring) + H2. Rationale: Deprotonation creates an aromatic, planar 6 pi-electron anion satisfying Hückel's 4n+2 rule.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Pyrrole is treated with Br2 in dioxane (0°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Pyrrole with Br2 in dioxane (0°C) yields 2-Bromopyrrole (substitution at C2). Rationale: Electrophilic attack at C2 generates a more resonance-stabilized intermediate (3 resonance structures) than C3.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with KNO3, H2SO4 / 300°C to yield 3-Nitropyridine (substitution at C3) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Pyridine reacts with KNO3, H2SO4 / 300°C to yield 3-Nitropyridine (substitution at C3). Rationale: Attack at C3 avoids a destabilizing resonance contributor with positive charge directly on electronegative nitrogen.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Naphthalene is treated with V2O5 / O2 / 400°C?
questions.explanation: Treating Naphthalene with V2O5 / O2 / 400°C yields Phthalic anhydride. Rationale: Catalytic vapor-phase oxidation cleaves one of the fused aromatic rings to yield phthalic anhydride.
